content:
Apple Cash's terms and conditions have just been updated, and Apple is notifying users of two changes that are about to take effect.

Apple Cash will soon begin requiring users to verify their identity when adding funds, and may enable "externally initiated funds transactions"

If you use Apple Cash, you may have just received — or will soon receive — an email notifying you of changes to the terms and conditions.

Apple partners with Green Dot Bank to provide the Apple Cash service, and the bank's revised terms page (available here) includes several important changes that Apple is highlighting in the email.

"First is about identity verification. Apple notes:"

"Another upcoming change involves 'externally initiated funds transactions.' Although a date has not yet been set, the new terms give Green Dot the ability to offer this feature. Apple writes:"

Another change Apple is highlighting in the email relates to the arbitration section of Green Dot's terms. Beyond Apple encouraging users to review the relevant changes, no specific updates are mentioned, as they involve users' rights and the dispute resolution process.

Have you noticed any other changes in the revised Apple Cash terms? Let us know in the comments.
